messages.content:
Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(a_0=1\) and the recurrence cannot produce \(0\) or \(-1\), every \(a_n\) is invertible modulo \(397\).

From
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397},
\]
we get
\[
\frac1{a_{n+1}} \equiv \frac{(a_n+1)^2}{a_n}
= a_n+2+\frac1{a_n}.
\]
Thus
\[
a_n \equiv \frac1{a_{n+1}}-\frac1{a_n}-2 \pmod{397}.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv
\left(\frac1{a_{2027}}-\frac1{a_0}\right)-2\cdot 2027.
\]
Since \(a_0=1\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv
\frac1{a_{2027}}-1-4054.
\]

Given \(a_{2026}=9\),
\[
a_{2027}\equiv \frac{9}{10^2}\pmod{397},
\]
so
\[
\frac1{a_{2027}}\equiv \frac{100}{9}\pmod{397}.
\]
Now \(9^{-1}\equiv 353\pmod{397}\), hence
\[
\frac{100}{9}\equiv 100\cdot 353\equiv 364\pmod{397}.
\]
Also \(1+4054=4055\equiv 85\pmod{397}\). Therefore
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n \equiv 364-85=279\pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
